newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends up on overseas buying.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends up on overseas buying.

text.p: Hong Kong's gold market ended Thursayy up from the previous New York close on buying from Japan, physical offtake, and short covering in afternoon trade from European customers, bullion dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$354.00/50 an ounce on Thursday against New York's US$352.25/75 close on Wednesday.
With gold in yen starting about 15 yen below its previous close, Japanese traders saw gold as an attractive buy, dealers said.
When Europe opened, customers were covering their short positions after the market failed to break through lower levels overnight in New York, dealers said.
Physical offtake also pushed the market slightly higher, dealers said.
But the direction remained slightly confused, with sentiment still leaning towards bearishness, dealers said.
"People don't have much of a clue where the market is going," said a dealer at an international bank, noting that few people were willing to establish fresh positions.
But the range had widened slightly from a tight 50 U.S. cent band to a few dollars, with resistance seen at $356.
Local gold ended HK$7 higher at HK$3,273 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to +1.00 from its previous fix at +0.01
